name: Fasting
overview: Scripture presents fasting as a solemn practice of abstaining from food and drink to seek God's guidance, express repentance, and intensify prayer, exemplified by Moses' forty-day fast on the mountain receiving the covenant (Exodus 24:18; 34:28; Deuteronomy 9:9, 18). Fasting often accompanies public or private affliction and urgent petitions, as seen when Israel fasted and prayed before the LORD during times of crisis (Judges 20:26) and when Ezra proclaimed a fast to seek a right way for the people (Ezra 8:21). This discipline humbles the believer and aligns the heart toward God, reinforcing the spiritual nature of fasting beyond mere physical abstinence.
